in_arabic.name: سلطانة
in_arabic.long_meaning: الاسم سلطانة مشتق من الكلمة العربية سلطان، وهو يُشير إلى المرأة التي تتمتع بالسلطة والقوة، وهو مصطلح يُستخدم في الإسلام لوصف المرأة التي تتمتع بالحكمة والقوة الروحية، كما يُشير إلى المرأة التي تتمتع بسلطة الروح والجسد

in_urdu.name: سلطانہ
in_urdu.meaning: عورت جو صاحب اختیار اور طاقت کی مالک ہو
in_urdu.long_meaning: اسم سلطانہ عربی زبان کے لفظ سلطان سے ماخوذ ہے، یہ عورت کی وہ صفت ہے جو اختیار اور طاقت کی مالک ہو، یہ اسلام میں عورت کی وہ عظمت ہے جو روحانی اور جسمانی دونوں طرح کی طاقت کی مالک ہو

in_hindi.name: सुल्ताना
in_hindi.meaning: महिला जो अधिकार और शक्ति की मालिक है
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाम सुल्ताना अरबी शब्द सुल्तान से लिया गया है, यह महिला की वह विशेषता है जो अधिकार और शक्ति की मालिक है, यह इस्लाम में महिला की वह महानता है जो आध्यात्मिक और शारीरिक दोनों तरह की शक्ति की मालिक है

in_pashto.name: سلطانه
in_pashto.meaning: ښځه چې واک او قدرت لرونکې وي

data.cultural_impact: The name Sultannah reflects the historical significance of powerful female rulers in Islamic civilization, who played important roles in politics, diplomacy, and governance. Some prominent examples include Queen Razia of the Delhi Sultanate (1236–1240 CE), who is considered the first woman to rule an Islamic empire, and Nur Jahan (1567–1645 CE), one of the most powerful empresses of the Mughal empire and wife of Emperor Jahangir. The name Sultannah reflects the rich tradition of strong and influential women in Islamic history, emphasizing the role of women in shaping Islamic civilizations.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sultannah carries intrinsic spiritual significance for women as it literally means 'female ruler'. It supports the belief that women can wield power and authority, not just in worldly matters, but also in their spiritual lives. The name encourages women to embrace their inner strength and leadership qualities and fulfill their roles as the 'queens' of their own souls and homes. It also underscores the fundamental principle of gender equality in Islam, as evident in verses such as "And of His Signs is that He created mates for you from yourselves, that you might find tranquility in them; and He put between you affection and mercy. Indeed, in that are signs for those who reflect." (Quran 30:21).
